AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND AND AIM
AbstractText.content: Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB) is an effective treatment for weight loss in patients with morbid obesity. However, few studies have assessed its long-term efficacy in super-obese patients. The study objective was to analyse the long-term effectiveness of RYGB and its effect on improvement of comorbidities after 10 years of follow-up, and to compare the results depending on baseline BMI (<50kg/m(2) vs ≥50kg/m(2)).

AbstractText.Label: PATIENTS AND METHODS
AbstractText.content: A retrospective study was conducted in 63 patients referred for RYGB with a 10-year or longer follow-up period. Mean BMI before surgery was 55kg/m(2).

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Mean BMI decreased to 38.1kg/m(2) at 10 years of follow-up. The success rates according to Reinhold criteria modified by Christou and to Biron's criteria were 30.2% and 54% respectively. The corresponding rates in super-obese patients were 21.4% and 57.1%. Significant, stable improvement was seen in diabetes, dyslipidemia, hypertension, and sleep apnea.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Sustained weight loss was achieved after gastric bypass, with a mean excess weight loss of 50.6% after 10 years despite the high prevalence of super-obesity. Comorbidity improvement was maintained.
